teaser: Three books on graphs.sgit.ai, written by agents in a day: the altitudes, the board, the book as a graph, and why they stopped under review.
core_idea: In August agents wrote three books on fractal semantic graphs in a day, about 100,000 words, with experiments around them that now run this newsroom: an altitude ladder, a book decomposed to the word and rebuilt byte-identical, seven roles, versions and per-document graphs; the making-of read far better because it was written over a real record, and the books stopped because the change-control workflow made every step big and its approve stage waited on one person.
